Definition: Distance from zero. The absolute value can never be negative.
Examples: For example, `abs(-1)|=17` and `abs(42)=42`.`

Definition: The perpendicular distance from the base of a geometric figure to the opposite vertex (or side if parallel).
The space between two intersecting lines, measured in degrees or radians.
A portion of the circumference of a circle. If the circle was a pizza, your slice would be a sector, and the crust on your slice would be an arc.
A straight line that is the limiting value of a curve; can be considered as tangent at infinity.
The bottom (and sometimes the top) of a 3-D geometric figure.
Examples: For example, the base of a cylinder is a circle.

Definition: (1) A quantity expressed as a sum or difference of two terms.
(2) A polynomial with two terms.
To divide a line, angle, or shape into two equal parts.

A functional relationship between two variables where a change in the value of one variable (the independent variable or “cause”) directly results in a change in the value of another variable (the dependent variable or “effect”).

the point from which all points on a circle are equidistant. The center is in the circle, but not on the circle. All the radii start at the center, and the center is the midpoint of every diameter. In the standard equation for a circle, the center is referred to with the coordinates `(h,k)`.
A straight line connecting two points on a curve.

The set of all points in a plane that are equidistant from a given point (aka, the center). A point is on the circle if it is on the circumference. A point is in the circle if it is in the area enclosed by the circumference.
The total linear distance around the outside of a circle.
A numerical or constant factor that multiplies a variable in an algebraic expression or equation.
The elements outside of a given set.
A number that is a mix of the real and the imaginary. It is given in the form `a+bi`, where `a` is the real part and `bi` is the imaginary part.
A type of interest that earns additional interest.
A 3-D shape with a circular base on the bottom and a point on the top. (Or you could turn it upside down and have the circle on the top and the point on the bottom.)

A way to describe the level of uncertainty when a statistic about a population is being estimated by a sampling from that population. The confidence interval gives an upper and lower boundary between which you are a certain percent sure the true value falls.
Examples: For example, Amy polled `100` people and asked them how they would vote in next week's election. `52%` of them said they would vote for her. As a result, she is `90%` sure that she will get between `47%` and `57%` of the vote on election day.

Definition: When two geometric figures are identical in shape and size, having equal corresponding sides and angles.
Two binomials in the form `(a+b)(a-b)`. When you multiply conjugates, you will get a difference of squares. When you multiply complex conjugates` (a+bi)(a-bi)`, the result will be a real number
In a row, without skipping over any items.
Examples: For example, `14`, `15`, and `16` are consecutive integers; `19`, `21`, and `23` are consecutive odd integers, and `/_A` and `/_B` would be consecutive angles in hexagon `ABCDEF`.

Definition: (1) The term of a polynomial that doesn't have a variable at all.
(2) A parameter in a function that will always hold the same value, even for different points on the function.
Examples: (1) For example, in the polynomial `15x^2-19x+7` the constant is `7`.
(2) For example, in the function `y=5x-9`, the variables are `x` and `y` while the constants are `5` and `-9`. If the function is written as `y=mx+b`, the constants are `m` and `b`.

Definition: Ordered pairs or sets of numbers, usually written as  `(x,y)`, that define the exact position of a point on a 2D plane or in space.

A way to describe the trend in bivariate data. In other words, if the line of best fit has a positive slope, there is a positive correlation, and if the line of best fit has a negative slope, there is a negative correlation. Correlation does not always suggest causation.

In a right triangle, the ratio between the side adjacent to a given angle and the hypotenuse. Usually abbreviated to “cos”, but please pronounce this as “cosine” not “cos”. `cosx=text(adjacent)/text(hypoteuse)`
A rectangular prism where all three dimensions are equal in length.
A 3-D geometric figure with two circular bases. This is the shape of a can or tube. The formula for volume is `V=pir^2h`.
Numerical or categorical information collected to analyze, summarize, and draw inferences, often presented in tables, graphs, or scenarios.
Getting smaller. A function is decreasing when, if you trace along the function from left to right, you are going in an downward direction.
(1) A way to describe a polynomial by giving the highest exponent.
(2) A unit used to measure an angle. A right angle has `90°`, a straight angle has `180°`, and a full circle has `360°`.
Examples: (1) For example `15x^7-12x^4+3x-1` is a `7^text(th)` degree polynomial.

Definition: The amount of money put into a bank account. This does not include any interest earned on that money.
Examples: For exmaple, Jack opens up a new bank account and makes an initial deposit of `$100`.

Definition: A line segment connecting two non-adjacent vertices (corners) of a polygon, passing through its interior.
The longest distance from one side of a circle to another. The diameter is twice the radius and will always go through the center of its circle.
Describes the arrangement, shape, spread, and center of a dataset, typically represented via graphs like histograms or box plots.

All the values of `x` you can use in a function. Most functions have an infinite domain; the exceptions are rational functions, where you have to make sure the denominator will not be zero, and radical functions, where you have to make sure the value under the square root is `>=0`.
Examples: For example, The domain of `f(x)=-7x^2-4` is infinite because you can plug in any `x` value at all and get an answer. However, the domain of `g(x)=(x-7)/(x+2)` is all real numbers except `x=-2` because if you try to plug in `-2` for `x`, you will get a zero in a denominator.

Definition: The individual items in a set.
Examples: For example, the set `{-7,7}` has two elements.

Definition: A mathematical statement that includes an equal sign.
Equal to, or the same as.
A superscript number indicating how many times to multiply a base number by itself.
Something that is getting smaller at an ever decreasing-rate. This is represented by a curve that starts off with a steep drop, but eventually levels off.
Examples: For example, starting with a value such as `300` and cutting it in half over and over which is modeled by the function `f(x)=300(1/2)^x`.

Definition: Something that is growing at an ever-increasing rate. This is represented by a curved line that starts off almost flat, but eventually gets very steep.
Examples: For example, starting with the number `5` and doubling it over and over which is modeled by the function `f(x)=5(2)^x`.

Definition: A mathematical statement consisting of numbers, variables, and/or operations that does not have an equal sign or inequality. Expressions cannot be solved; they can only be simplified.
An integer or algebraic expression that divides another number or expression evenly, leaving no remainder.
An acronym that describes the process of multiplying two binomials. It stands for Firsts, Outers, Inners, Lasts.
The number of times a specific value, data point, or event occurs within a dataset.

A mathematical description of the relationship between two variables. Typically, `x` is the input, and `f(x)` is the output. For a relation to be a function, there must be exactly one value of `f(x)` for each value of `x`.
Examples: For example, `f(x)=2x-1` is an example of a linear function; `f(x)=x^2-8x+7` is an example of a quadratic function, and the equation of a circle such as `(x-2)^2+y^2=81` isn't a function at all because it fails the vertical line test.

Definition: A visual representation of the relationship between two variables. On the SAT, you will be analyzing graphs of functions and relations that are shown on the xy-plane.
The measurement from the bottom to the top, along a vertical line.
The side of a right triangle that is opposite the right angle. It will always be the longest side of the right triangle.

A value that includes `i`, which is equal to `sqrt(-1)` (meaning `i^2=-1`). Imaginary numbers can't be graphed on a number line or coordinate plane, but often result as solutions when using the quadratic formular
Getting larger. A function is increasing when, if you trace along the function from left to right, you are going in an upward direction.
A statement describing the relationship between two expressions. There are 5 inequalities in math: `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, and `!=`.
Making logical, data-driven conclusions about a larger population based on data from a sample.
All whole numbers and their opposites. Integers can be positive or negative, but cannot be fractions or have decimals.
Examples: For example, `0`, `5`, and `-15` are integers but `1/2`, `5.6, and `sqrt(2)` are not.

Definition: The points at which the graph of a function crosses over one of the axes. The y-intercept will have coordinates `(0,y)` and the x-intercept, `(x,0)`. Therefore, if you have the equation of the function, you can always find the intercepts by setting the opposite variable equal to zero.

The money a bank will give as compensation for saving money at their institution. Interest is a percentage of  savings that is typically given on an annual basis, and we represent it with the variable `r`. Simple interest does not earn more interest, while compounded interest gains even more interest.
The point(s), values, or elements common to two or more sets, lines, or graphs.
A continuous range of real numbers between two specific endpoints, defining a subset of the number line.
Decimal expansions that are non-terminating (never end) and non-repeating (never form a repeating pattern).
A trapezoid where the two non-parallel sides are congruent.
A triangle with two equal sides. Isosceles triangles will have two congruent base angles and one different vertex angle. Isosceles right triangles will be `45-45-90` triangles.
A geometric figure that extends infinitely in two directions and does not change direction.
A line drawn on a scatterplot to show the general trend of the data. The slope of your line of best fit would tell you if there is a positive or negative correlation to the data.
Aa relationship that has a constant slope. Equations in the form `y=mx+b` are linear.
The inverse of an exponential function, defining the power to which a base (`b`) must be raised to equal a given number (`a`).

A way to describe the level of uncertainty when a statistic about a population is being estimated by a sample from that population. The margin of error can be easily converted to a confidence interval, and vice versa.
Examples: For example, Amy polled 100 people and asked them how they would vote in next week's election. `52%` of them said they would vote for her. So, she estimates she will get `52%` of the vote with a margin of error of `+-5%`.

Definition: (1) The largest value in a set of data.
(2) The y-value of the highest point in a function.

A statistic calculated by adding up all the numbers in a set and dividing by how many values were in that set. The mean is also called the average and describes the center of the data. As compared to the median, the mean is more sensitive to outliers.

A statistic arrived at by putting the data in ascending order and selecting the middle number. If there are an even number of data points, the mean is calculated by adding the two numbers in the center and then dividing by zero. As compared to the mean, the median is less sensitive to outliers.
(1) The smallest value in a set of data.
(2) The y-value of the lowest point in a function.
A mathematical equation that describes how variables relate to each other in the real world.
Examples: The model `H=1.88L+32.02` can be used by archeologists to estimate a person's total height (`H`) from the length of the femur (`L`), where `H` and `L` are both in inches.

Definition: A possible result of a single trial of an experiment.
A number or numbers in a set that just don't seem to belong with all the other numbers because they are much larger or much smaller than the rest of the group.
Examples: For example, in the set `{5,52,58,59,62,71,80}, `5` is an outlier.

Definition: The “U” shaped curve that results from graphing a quadratic function.
In geometry, two lines in the same plane that will never intersect. In coordinate geometry, two lines that have equal slopes. In a system of equations, two lines that have no solution.
The expression of a decimal or fraction as a number out of `100`.
Examples: For example, the decimal `0.5` and the fraction `1/2` can be represented as the percentage `50%`.

Definition: The total distance around the outside edge of a two-dimensional shape, calculated by adding the lengths of all its sides.
In geometry, two lines in a plane that meet at a right angle. In coordinate geometry, two lines whose slopes are opposite reciprocals.
An irrational number that represents the ratio between the circumference of a circle and its diameter. It is usually rounded to `3.14` or represented as the fraction `22/7`.
A mathematical function that is the sum of a number of terms.
All of the elements in a group.
A 3D solid with two identical, parallel polygonal bases connected by rectangular or parallelogram side faces.
Measures the likelihood of an event occurring, expressed as a number between `0` (impossible) and `1` (certain).
The result of multiplication.
Examples: For example, the product of `5` and `6` is `30`.

Definition: An equation stating that two ratios or fractions are equal, written as `a/b=c/d`.
A 3-D geometric shape that has a polygonal base and comes to a point at the top. The sides are all triangles. The formula for the volume of a rectangular pyramid is `V=1/3lwh`.
An equation relating the three sides of a right triangle. Specifically, it is `a^2+b^2=c^2` where `a` and `b` are the legs and `c` is the hypotenuse.
Sets of three integers that satisfy the Pythagorean theorem.
Examples: For example, `3-4-5` and `5-12-13`.

Definition: Any of the four areas into which the `xytext(-plane)` is divided by the `x` and `y` coordinate axes.
The result of division.
Examples: The quotient of `20` and `5` is `4`.

Definition: A unit of measurement for angles. A right angle is `pi/2` radians, a straight angle is `pi` radians, and a whole circle is `2pi` radians.
The distance between the center of any circle and any point on that circle. The radius is half of the diameter.

(1) A statistic calculated by subtracting the smallest value from the largest value. It is a very simple way to describe the amount of spread in a set of data. Finding the standard deviation would be a more involved and more accurate method of describing the spread.
(2) All possible y-values for a given function.
Examples: (2) For example, the range of `f(x)=x^2+7` is from `7` to positive infinity.

Definition: A way to describe the comparison of two separate measurements, such as in miles per hour. If you are working in the context of a `D=RT` question, `R` is the rate. If you are working in the context of a coordinate geometry, rate will be the slope of the line expressed as a positive number preceded by the word “increasing” or “decreasing.”
A comparison of two numbers, usually written as a fraction or in the form `a:b`.
Examples: For example, If there are `2` watermelons and `15` pumpkins in a field, then the ratio of watermelons to pumpkins is `2:15`.

Definition: any number that can be expressed as a fraction `p/q`, where `p` and `q` are integers and `q!=0`.
Any number that can be located on a number line. All positives, negatives, decimals, and zero are real numbers. The only numbers that aren't real are imaginary numbers.
A `4` sided figure with `4` right angles. Find the perimeter by adding up the 4 sides, and find the area by multiplying length by width.
A 3-D figure with a length, width, and height, and where all the angles are right. If the three dimensions are all equal, it is a cube. The formula for volume of a rectangular prism is `V=lwh`.
A geometric shape where all the sides are equal, and all the angles are equal. A regular triangle is an equilateral triangle. A regular quadrilateral is a square.
The number “left over” when you divide two numbers.
Examples: For example, dividing `13` by `5` equal `2` with a remainder of `3`. (`(5xx2=10)+3=13`)

Definition: (1) An angle of exactly `90°`, or a shape that includes an angle of `90°`.
A cone where the point is directly above (or directly below) the center of the circular base. The formula for volume of a right circular cone is `V=1/3pir^2h`.
A trapezoid where one of the sizes is perpendicular to the bases.
(1) A number that when multiplied by itself a certain number of times results in the given value.
(2) Another word for the zeros or x-intercepts of a polynomial function. Find the roots by setting the equation equal to zero and solving.
Examples: (1) For example, the square root of `100` is `10` and the `5^text(th)` root of `32` is `2`.

Definition: A subset of a population.
Examples: For example, Makenzie wants to know how the kids in her school feel about wearing uniforms, so she talks to a sample of `20` students randomly selected from the student body.

Definition: The process a researcher uses to collect data from a portion of a population. This could be accomplished by making observations, running an experiment, or conducting a survey. A good sampling method is one where the participants (or data points) are randomly selected and where every member of the population has a chance of being selected.
Causes an equation to be true.
A method of displaying bivariate data by graphing each pair of numbers as a point with an `x` and `y` coordinate.
A portion of the area of a circle. If the circle was a pizza, your slice would be a sector, and the crust on your slice would be an arc.
An ordered list of numbers (terms) following a specific rule, usually denoted as `a_1`, `a_2`, `a_3`, ..., `a_n`.
When two shapes have the exact same shape but differ in size, or one is a mirror image of the other.
Two triangles that are the same shape, but not necessarily the same size. Their angles will be equal, but their sides will be proportional.
A type of interest that only applies to the initial deposit.
Rewriting an expression into a shorter, more compact form without changing its value.

In a right triangle, the ratio between the side opposite a given angle and the hypotenuse. Usually abbreviated to “sin”, but please, for the sake of math teacher's everywhere, pronounce this as “sine” not “sin”. `sinx=text(oppositie)/text(hypotenuse)`
The ratio of vertical change (“rise”) to horizontal change (“run”) between two points.
a mnemonic to help you remember three important formulas in trigonometry: `sinx=text(oppositie)/text(hypotenuse)`, `cosx=text(adjacent)/text(hypoteuse)`, and `tanx=text(opposite)/text(adjacent)`.
(1) The value of a variable that makes an equation true.
(2) The point(s) at which the graphs of two or more functions cross.
Examples: (1) For example, the solution of `5x-7=-2` is `x=1`.

Definition: All possible values of the variable.
Examples: For example, if `abs(x)=7`, then `x` can equal `7` or `-7`, and the solution set is `{-7,7}`.

Definition: Triangles with angles of `30°-60°-90°` or with angles of `45°-45°-90°`. These triangles are special because if you are given the length of any one of the sides, you can figure out the other two sides.
The set of all points in 3-D space that are equidistant from a given point. That given point is the center of the sphere. The formula for the volume of a sphere is `V=4/3pir^3`.

A statistic that describes how spread out the data is. If low then the data are gathered (or “clumped”) close to the mean; if high then there are data points pretty far to the left and the right of the center.
Data analysis, focusing on measures of center (mean, median, mode) and spread (range, standard deviation) to describe datasets.
The result of adding two or more values.

Multiple equations for which there are multiple unknown variables. If `x` and `y` are both unknowns, you need to have two equations to solve for them. Solutions can be found using elimination or substitution methods.
Data that is organized into rows and columns.

(1) In a right triangle, the ratio between the side opposite a given angle and side adjacent to that angle. Keep in mind the adjacent side will never be the hypotenuse. `tanx=text(opposite)/text(adjacent)`
(2) A line that touches a circle but doesn't go inside the circle, meaning that it is perpendicular to the radius of the circle.

A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides, called the bases. If one of the sides is perpendicular to the bases, it is a right trapezoid. If the two non-parallel sides are congruent, it is an isosceles trapezoid.
The general direction, pattern, or relationship between two variables in a scatter plot or data.
A 2-D shape with three sides and three angles. The three angles will always add up to `180°`.
This is the result of trying to divide a number by zero, which results in a number that is infinitely large. In terms of a graph, this is the slope of a vertical line.
The set of elements that are in either one of two given sets.
Examples: For example, the union of `{1,2,3}` and `{3,4,5}` is `{1,2,3,4,5}`.

Definition: Numbers that the variable is able to represent.
Examples: For example, the values of `x` that satisfy `x^2=9` are `3` and `-3`.

Definition: A symbol or letter (commonly `x`, `y`, or `f`) used as a placeholder to represent an unknown number or a quantity that can change.
A corner point where two or more lines, sides, or edges meet.
An easy way to tell if a graph is a function. If you can draw a vertical line that passes through the graph in more than one place, then it's not a function.
A measurement of how much space is inside a 3-D figure. The units that describe volume will be cubic (`text(in)^3`, `text(ft)^3`, text(cm)^3`) or volume specific (`text(gallon)`, `text(liter)`).
An objects' mass times the acceleration due to gravity. Common units for weight are pounds (`text(lbs)`) and Newtons (`text(N)`).
The horizontal baseline in the coordinate xy-plane.
A two dimensional system in which the exact location of any point can be described by giving its distance from the baseline horizontal and vertical axes.
The vertical baseline in the coordinate xy-plane.
Another word for the roots or x-intercepts of a polynomial function, which are found by setting the function equal to zero and solving.
